subject: Hosted API renewal + expansion: tier regrade & burst handling
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T15:23:00Z
Subject: Hosted API renewal + expansion: draft proposal and next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a draft renewal that combines the 12-month hosted commit you asked for plus the two-tier burst allowance we discussed. High level:

- Baseline monthly commit: 1.2B tokens (migrated from current 600M)
- Burst pocket: 300M tokens/month (soft-throttle after 95%)
- Unit pricing tiers adjusted for uplifting volume (see attachment)

Can we lock in a 30-minute call on Wednesday (10/14) to walk pricing and the SLA clauses? Procurement loops — please loop in Sam or procurement@ if there are any contract-level constraints.

Attachments: EcomPulse_HostedRenewal_Proposal_v1.pdf, ecompulse_usage_q3_breakdown.csv

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal + expansion: draft proposal and next steps

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the draft. A few quick things from our side before the call:

- Procurement wants the burst pocket to be billable only if sustained for more than 24 hours (we need protection against short spikes).
- Can you add an ops note on hot-cache behavior and KV cache reuse — our product team is concerned about latency on microburst patterns.
- Also curious if we can phase the monthly commit (800M -> 1.2B) with a mid-term review at month 6.

Looping in Sam (cc) and procurement@ for visibility. We'll join the Wed call but might ask to push until Thurs depending on internal calendar.

Thanks,
Alice Moreno
Head of Platform, EcomPulse
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T11:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal + expansion: draft proposal and next steps

Thanks Alice — quick technical clarifications below that we can fold into the SOW:

- Burst billing threshold: we can implement a 24-hour sustained window before charging the burst pocket. That will require an explicit labeling of 'sustained burst' in the billing pipeline (ops change).
- Latency mitigation: recommend enabling prefix KV caching and increasing continuous-batch size to lower p95 during microbursts. Expect p95 improvement ~20-30ms in our tests for similar workloads.
- Phased commit: fine to structure as 6-month step-up (800M for 1-6 months, 1.2B thereafter) with an optional quality & cost review at month 6.

I attached a small usage extract for reference (ecompulse_usage_q3_breakdown.csv). Happy to present with Hannah on the technical slide for the renewal call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T08:12:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API renewal + expansion: draft proposal and next steps

Ben/Laura —

Forwarding thread with EcomPulse. They want: 24-hour sustained-burst billing, phased commit (800M -> 1.2B month 7), and explicit latency mitigation ops notes. Please advise:

- Commercial: can we offer a stepped pricing ladder for month 1-6 vs month 7+? Any margin constraints we should flag?
- Legal/Contracts: is 24-hour sustained burst billable language straightforward to capture?

I'll hold the client call until we have a commercial and legal pass.

Hannah
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API renewal + expansion: draft proposal and next steps

Hannah —

We can do a stepped commercial: pricing below (baseline monthly commit pricing, USD):

- Months 1-6: baseline 800M tokens at $0.0016/token equivalent (intro uplift discount)
- Months 7-12: baseline 1.2B tokens at $0.00145/token equivalent
- Burst pocket (300M): $0.0022/token only if sustained >24 hours (measured by rolling window)

Other terms: 12-month term, 30-day termination notice after month 9, annualized billing preferred (we can support quarterly invoicing if required). We will include the 24-hour sustained-burst language in SOW and a described billing rule.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1187
DocuSign placeholder: https://docusign.com/sign?doc=EP-Renewal-v1

If this looks good, Laura can coordinate legal to generate the SOW with the sustained-burst clause and pricing ladder.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@ecompulse.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ecompulse.com, Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal + expansion: draft proposal and next steps

Hannah/Ben —

Thanks for the updated commercial and the clarified burst rules. Procurement has reviewed and is comfortable with the 24-hour sustained-burst definition and the stepped commit schedule. Two asks before signature:

1) Confirm that the soft-throttle threshold (95%) will not lead to customer-visible errors and that Redwood will provide a mitigation runbook if we see elevated 5xx rates.
2) Please confirm invoicing cadence. Procurement prefers annualized billing but can accept quarterly if coupled with a 30-day payment term.

If you confirm these points I'll route the DocuSign to legal and we can get the PO over next week.

Regards,
Sam Ortiz
Head of Procurement, EcomPulse
